label: Eluta.ca
terms_note: Canadian employer-site aggregator; apply on origin.

endpoints.call: Advanced Search) can be fetched as RSS 2.0 (GET https://www.eluta.ca/rss?q=<keywords>&l=<location>&limit=N, also fmt=j for JSON-P) — live-verified ('Eluta: developer jobs', PyRSS2Gen).
endpoints.notes: from the docs / live response read on 2026-09-05

reference.limits: Free of charge, no key, no published rate limit; Developer rules: use the data to 'create good things' (personal or commercial is fine), no adult / illegal / hateful sites, no made-for-AdSense spam pages; usage is subject to Eluta's standard Terms of Service. Free of charge, no key, no published rate limit; robots.txt disallows /rss? for crawlers (the feed is meant for developers, not search engines) and Disallow: / for unlisted agents.

adapter.terms: Eluta developers page: 'No adult or illegal sites', 'No spam pages'; the feed is free of charge.

search.note: Eluta offers its search 'free of charge using either RSS ... or our OpenSearch API': 'You can create an RSS feed for any search on Eluta' (example /rss?fmt=j&q=French&l=Toronto+ON&limit=5; fmt=j is a JavaScript snippet, so it is not sent and the RSS 2.0 form is used). q is the keyword search and l the location (e.g. 'Toronto ON'); the feed returns the first 20 matches and has no page parameter, so page is not sent. employer, location and a highlighted snippet (description, HTML) are per item; id is the posting link. Eluta's policy: 'You may not check each RSS feed more than 2 times per hour'. Past it the feed answers 200 with a channel titled 'Eluta: Too Many Requests' and one notice item; the runtime turns that into a rate_limited error instead of a posting, and the client-side limit is one call per 100 s. Responses come through a squid cache (Cache-Control max-age 3 h, Vary: User-Agent), so a feed can be up to 3 h old (live check 2026-09-26).

not_offered.me: No credentials to verify ('auth: none'): the feed is public and has no account endpoint.
not_offered.get_posting: The feed has no per-item endpoint (each posting's url is an HTML page); search returns the whole record in raw.
not_offered.apply: No application endpoint: the feed only lists postings; candidates apply on each posting's url (employer page / e-mail).
not_offered.list_messages: No messaging API; the only machine-readable interface is the public job feed.

live_check.notes: fixed: past 'not more than 2 times per hour' per feed, the RSS answers 200 with a 'Too Many Requests' item that was returned as a posting; now a rate_limited error, limit one call per 100 s. Upstream squid cache (max-age 3 h, Vary: User-Agent) can serve different snapshots; also: next_page now null (no page parameter); all read tools answered, schema-valid
